children: The lender is strengthening its frontline workforce and distribution network, with plans to open over 100 branches in the second half of FY27

IndusInd Bank has added approximately 4,300 employees across its operations, primarily in sourcing roles, as the private sector lender strengthens its frontline workforce and prepares to expand its branch network in the second half of the 2026-27 financial year.

The hiring expansion forms part of the bank's broader strategy to strengthen its sales and sourcing capabilities, improve market penetration and support business growth. The lender plans to open more than 100 branches during the second half of FY27, with a focus on underpenetrated markets and geographies where expansion had previously been limited.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Rajiv Anand outlined the workforce expansion during the bank's second-quarter earnings discussion on October 23, highlighting the importance of strengthening frontline capacity alongside its distribution network.

The bank is also accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence across its operations. More than 50 per cent of its employees are using generative AI chatbots, with over half of these active users accessing the tools daily. The initiative is aimed at improving employee productivity and supporting routine business activities.

IndusInd Bank has additionally introduced six voice-bot programmes and identified 12 more customer and employee processes where conversational AI could be deployed. The bank is evaluating these applications to assess their potential operational benefits before expanding their use.
The simultaneous focus on workforce expansion and technology adoption reflects the lender's efforts to strengthen its physical presence while improving operational efficiency and customer engagement.

On the financial front, IndusInd Bank reported a net profit of Rs 1,242 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 437 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. The improvement was accompanied by stronger business momentum and better asset quality.
As of September 30, 2026, the bank operated 3,139 branches and banking outlets, supported by 2,773 ATMs. Its customer base stood at approximately 42 million.

The planned branch expansion and additional hiring indicate a renewed emphasis on frontline capacity and physical distribution as IndusInd Bank seeks to strengthen its presence in India's competitive banking sector.
